battle.name: 哥倫比亞-秘魯戰爭
battle.brief: 中文維基「戰爭列表」所列的1931年哥倫比亞-秘魯戰爭，由哥倫比亞與秘魯在亞馬遜地區的邊界爭議引發，交戰主要集中於萊蒂西亞一帶。條目選列的Gatling gun加特林機槍於1860年列裝，是各國陸軍武器體系中用於火力支援的早期旋轉式重機槍。

kit.name: 加特林機槍
kit.history: Gatling gun屬早期多管旋轉式重機槍，通常由炮組集中操作，配置於步兵營的火力支援點，以高射速提供壓制，並與輕機槍及火炮協同。

countries: 1931年的哥倫比亞—秘魯戰爭，是哥倫比亞共和國與秘魯共和國之間一場通常被視為未經正式宣戰的邊境戰事。戰區位於哥倫比亞南部、秘魯洛雷托與亞馬遜上游交會的Putumayo河流域；雙方的政治與軍事重鎮都遠離前線，真正被爭奪的是未設界碑的邊警哨、海關站、渡口、河道以及通往Iquitos的水路。一般以1931年2月14日前後，哥倫比亞邊防巡邏越過暫定界線、攻取秘魯邊警哨作為開端。秘魯由Iquitos調派地面分隊與內河艇，並以飛機攻擊哥方沿河陣地。數月的點狀交火後，秘魯把爭議提交國際聯盟，兩國同意以仲裁及混合劃界取代進一步會戰。
countriesEn: The Colombia–Peru War of 1931 was a border conflict between the Republic of Colombia and the Republic of Peru, generally regarded as a war without a formal declaration. The theater lay in the Putumayo River basin, where southern Colombia met Loreto and the upper Amazon. Both countries’ political and military centers were far from the front; what was actually contested was a group of unmarked police posts, customs stations, landing places, river channels, and routes leading to Iquitos. The opening is generally dated to about February 14, 1931, when a Colombian border patrol crossed the provisional line and seized a Peruvian police post. Peru dispatched ground detachments and river craft from Iquitos, while aircraft attacked Colombian positions along the river. After several months of isolated engagements, Peru referred the dispute to the League of Nations, and both states accepted arbitration and mixed boundary commissions instead of further large-scale combat.
people: 最高政治層由哥倫比亞總統Enrique Olaya Herrera與秘魯的Luis Miguel Sánchez Cerro主持；後者自1930年起掌握秘魯國家權力，並於1931年7月就任憲制總統。實際作戰命令則經由兩國陸軍部、邊防司令部與地方駐軍逐級下達。哥倫比亞方面主要涉及南部邊防司令部、Putumayo沿線駐哨及航空分隊；秘魯方面則由Iquitos駐軍、洛雷托行政與軍事當局、亞馬遜內河艦艇人員及航空隊共同執行。參與者包括營、連級指揮官、巡邏隊長、士官、通信兵、工兵、醫護、飛行員與艇隊人員。國際聯盟理事會、國際常設法院及後來的混合劃界技術人員則進入外交與測量環節。現存材料常把不同小隊的行動合併敘述，因此較可靠的是交代各單位功能，而不是虛構一名包辦全戰役的單一指揮官。
peopleEn: At the highest political level, Colombian President Enrique Olaya Herrera and Luis Miguel Sánchez Cerro, who had headed Peru since 1930 and became its constitutional president in July 1931, oversaw the crisis. Operational orders, however, passed through the two war ministries, border commands, and regional garrisons. Colombia’s effort involved the southern border command, outposts along the Putumayo, and aviation detachments. Peru drew on the Iquitos garrison, Loreto’s civil and military authorities, Amazon river personnel, and its air force. Participants included battalion and company commanders, patrol leaders, noncommissioned officers, signallers, engineers, medical personnel, pilots, and boat crews. The League of Nations Council, the Permanent Court of International Justice, and later mixed-boundary survey personnel entered the diplomatic and cartographic phases. Surviving accounts often merge the actions of separate detachments, so the safer account identifies each unit’s function rather than inventing one commander who directed the entire war.
kits: 1931年的裝備並非兩軍完全相同，但可核對的代表性項目包括Mauser M1895步槍，口徑為7.65×54mmR；Lee-Enfield系列也是重要武器，哥倫比亞曾使用Short Magazine Lee-Enfield Mk III，秘魯則有不同批次的Lee-Enfield改裝型。秘魯重機槍清冊可見Schwarzlose M1907/12與Maxim Model 1912；炮兵方面，兩國均曾列裝75公厘口徑野戰炮，包括Schneider-Canet Mle 1919。步兵還配有Mills No. 5手榴彈。航空兵力方面，秘魯在Iquitos一帶使用Curtiss F-11C Falcon，哥倫比亞則有Douglas O-2M及Fokker F.VII/3m可供偵察、聯絡與支援。河上行動依靠吃水淺的內河砲艇、汽艇、貨船與自製划艇，並非大型軍艦直接進入支流。7.65mm與.303 British步槍彈不可互換，機槍彈、75公厘炮彈和航空燃料又各有供應線；步槍便於分隊攜帶，重機槍、炮彈與燃料則依賴騾馬、舟艇及飛機，因此任何一個前進哨站都必須與後方補給保持聯繫。
kitsEn: The two armies did not have identical inventories, but representative weapons listed by 1931 included the Mauser Model 1895 chambered in 7.65×54mmR. Lee-Enfield rifles were also important: Colombia had used the Short Magazine Lee-Enfield Mk III, while Peru held several converted Lee-Enfield variants. Peru’s heavy-machine-gun inventory included the Schwarzlose Model 1907/12 and Maxim Model 1912. For artillery, both states had employed 75 mm field guns, notably the Schneider-Canet Model 1919. Infantry also carried Mills No. 5 hand grenades. In aviation, Peru operated the Curtiss F-11C Falcon around Iquitos, while Colombia had the Douglas O-2M and Fokker F.VII/3m available for reconnaissance, liaison, and support. River movement depended on shallow-draft gunboats, motor launches, cargo boats, and dugout canoes rather than on large warships entering the tributaries. The 7.65 mm and .303 British rifle rounds were not interchangeable, while machine-gun ammunition, 75 mm shells, and aviation fuel had separate supply lines. Rifles were portable, but heavy guns, shells, and fuel required mule trains, boats, or aircraft, so every advanced post had to remain connected to its rear supply system.
tactics: 最初的軍事動作是一場沿邊境巡邏路線展開的奪點，而不是直取Iquitos或跨越整個亞馬遜盆地的全面進攻。哥倫比亞分隊沿Putumayo河及森林小徑接近秘魯哨站，以突然占領、封閉通道和奪取文件或地圖控制局部地形；秘魯則利用Iquitos作補給中心，以內河艇輸送小股反擊部隊，再由航空隊攻擊碼頭、營地及林間空地。前線因此不是連續壕溝，而是由若干河灣、渡口、林徑出口和警哨組成的點狀網絡。雙方都知道守住登陸點與補給道路，比控制大片無人森林更重要。交火多在數十公尺能見度內發生，機槍集中封鎖小徑和岸坡，炮兵即使運到前線，也因目標分散及觀測困難而難以發揮。秘魯飛機造成短暫混亂與破壞，卻不能單獨消滅分散在林中的哥軍。哥倫比亞若把前哨推得太遠，糧食、藥品與彈藥便會拉長；秘魯若反覆沿同一河道追擊，也會受到雨季、河水漲落、熱帶病及艇員疲勞限制。雙方後來都把行動重點收束到既有哨站、渡口和補給線，而沒有把戰役擴展成沿整條邊界推進的大會戰。
tacticsEn: The opening military operation was a raiding movement along the border routes, not an advance aimed directly at Iquitos or a general crossing of the Amazon basin. Colombian detachments approached Peruvian posts by the Putumayo River and forest trails, relying on sudden seizure, control of crossings, and the capture of records or maps. Peru used Iquitos as its supply center, moved small counterattacking forces by river craft, and employed aircraft against landing places, camps, and clearings in the forest. The front was therefore not a continuous trench line but a chain of river bends, crossings, trail entrances, and police posts. Both sides understood that control of landing places and supply routes mattered more than possession of large areas of empty jungle. Firing often occurred within a few dozen metres of visibility, with machine guns covering trails and riverbanks. Even when artillery reached the forward area, dispersed targets and difficult observation limited its effect. Peruvian aircraft created short-lived disruption and damage but could not destroy a Colombian force dispersed among the trees. If Colombia pushed its outposts too far forward, food, medicine, and ammunition had to travel farther; repeated Peruvian counterattacks by the same river route were constrained by the rains, changing water levels, tropical illness, and fatigue among boat crews. Both sides later concentrated on existing posts, crossings, and supply lines rather than attempting to extend the campaign into a continuous front along the whole frontier.
data: 可核對的時間與地理骨架如下。1931年2月14日前後，哥倫比亞邊防巡邏越過未標示的界線，攻取Putumayo河上游邊境帶的一座秘魯邊警與稅務哨；相關行動集中在Taruca河口、Puerto Ocampo周邊及連接森林營地的路網。哥方把Puerto Ocampo一帶當作南區支撐點，秘方則從下游Iquitos沿Putumayo河逆流調動地面隊與內河艇。接下來數週，秘魯航空隊攻擊哥方沿河陣地，地面反擊與短暫奪哨交錯發生，若干前哨曾數度易手，但始終沒有出現任何一方直取Iquitos或突破對方整條補給線的局面。到1931年稍後，戰線大致凍結在原有哨站附近。秘魯同年向國際聯盟提出交涉，兩國在1932至1933年間接受仲裁與混合劃界程序。1933年1月24日簽署的《里約議定書》建立多個混合委員會，處理Putumayo、Tabatinga等邊界段落；後續測量持續多年，直到1971年才完成亞馬遜邊界的最後劃界。關於傷亡，現有資料只有零散戰報、傷員返送紀錄和機關彙報，沒有可交叉核驗的雙方總表，因此不能列出精確陣亡或受傷總數。
dataEn: The verifiable chronology and geography can be set out as follows. Around February 14, 1931, a Colombian border patrol crossed the unmarked boundary and seized a Peruvian police and customs post in the upper Putumayo frontier zone. The operation was concentrated around the mouth of the Taruca River, the Puerto Ocampo area, and the trail network connecting forest camps. Colombia treated the Puerto Ocampo vicinity as a southern support point, while Peru moved troops and river craft upstream from Iquitos. During the following weeks, Peruvian aircraft attacked Colombian positions along the river, ground counterattacks and brief seizures of posts alternated, and several forward positions changed hands more than once. Neither side approached Iquitos directly or broke the other’s entire supply line. By later in 1931, the front had largely frozen around the existing posts. Peru referred the matter to the League of Nations that same year, and the two states accepted arbitration and mixed-boundary procedures during 1932 and 1933. The Rio Protocol of January 24, 1933, established several mixed commissions to address boundary sections including Putumayo and Tabatinga. Survey work continued for years, and the Amazon boundary was not finally demarcated until 1971. On casualties, the surviving record consists only of fragmentary reports, evacuation lists, and administrative returns; there is no cross-verifiable total for either side, so no exact killed or wounded figure can responsibly be stated.
cause: 衝突根源不是一場突然出現的全面戰爭，而是哥倫比亞與秘魯在亞馬遜地區長期未能完成的劃界。兩國承接自西班牙殖民時期及十九世紀條約的邊界描述往往只寫到河流、支流或山脊，Putumayo下游的實際航路、島嶼與小支流則沒有連續界碑；後來的雙方佔哨、海關巡查與地方管轄又形成不同控制線。1926年的和平、友好、航行與通商條約推動混合委員會及國際程序處理邊界，國際常設法院1930年的諮詢意見雖處理部分爭段，卻沒有為整個亞馬遜前線畫出無爭議界線。兩國對條約文字、河流分水線與實際控制應採何種標準遂有不同解釋。1931年初，雙方巡邏在Taruca河口、Puerto Ocampo周邊及通往秘魯哨站的林徑相遇；究竟是哥軍越線攻哨、祕魯先射擊或雙方同時越過暫定線，細節在流傳紀錄中不一致。能確定的是，哥軍隨後奪取秘魯哨站並占據河岸，而秘魯將此視為主權入侵，遂把原本的管轄爭端升級為武裝衝突。
causeEn: The conflict did not arise from a suddenly conceived general war. It grew from a boundary that Colombia and Peru had long failed to demarcate in the Amazon. The two countries inherited descriptions drawn from Spanish colonial arrangements and nineteenth-century treaties that often referred only to rivers, tributaries, or ridges. The actual navigation channels, islands, and minor streams of the lower Putumayo had no continuous boundary markers, while later police posts, customs patrols, and local administration created different lines of control. The 1926 Treaty of Peace, Friendship, Navigation and Commerce promoted mixed commissions and international procedures for the frontier. Although the Permanent Court of International Justice issued an advisory opinion in 1930 dealing with part of the dispute, it did not establish an uncontested line for the entire Amazon front. Colombia and Peru consequently interpreted the treaty wording, watershed principle, and effective control differently. In early 1931 patrols met around the Taruca river mouth, the Puerto Ocampo area, and trails leading to Peruvian posts. Whether Colombian troops first crossed the line, Peruvian guards opened fire, or both sides violated the provisional boundary is not consistent across the surviving accounts. What is clear is that Colombian troops then seized a Peruvian post and occupied the riverbank, while Peru treated the action as a violation of sovereignty, turning a jurisdictional dispute into armed conflict.
impact: 軍事上的影響有限而清楚：秘魯保住了Iquitos、內河航運與航空支援中心，哥倫比亞則維持Taruca河口及Puerto Ocampo附近的遠前哨，但雙方都未能迫使對方全面退讓，也沒有摧毀對方的邊防體系。短暫奪哨、機槍伏擊、飛機攻擊、森林行軍、舟艇事故與熱帶病均造成零散損失，然而可靠總數並不存在，若寫出任何精確陣亡數都會超出證據。較長遠的影響發生在外交與行政層面：兩國不再只靠前線哨站解釋邊界，而接受國際聯盟介入、仲裁和混合測量，使邊界爭議進入可以逐段核對的程序。戰役也顯示，亞馬遜邊防不能只依賴地面巡邏；內河船、航空偵察、飛機運補和分散式哨站必須互相配合，而武器與糧食的分別供應會直接限制前進速度。最終結果並未由戰場決定，秘魯首先提出的國際化程序，反而把軍事接觸轉化為後續劃界委員會的工作。
impactEn: The military effect was limited but clear. Peru retained Iquitos, its inland river network, and its aviation support center, while Colombia maintained forward posts near the Taruca river mouth and Puerto Ocampo. Neither side compelled a comprehensive retreat or destroyed the other’s frontier organization. Brief seizures of posts, machine-gun ambushes, aircraft attacks, movement through forest, river accidents, and tropical illness all produced scattered losses, but no reliable aggregate exists; any precise death toll would exceed the evidence. The more durable effect occurred at the diplomatic and administrative level. The two governments stopped relying only on frontier outposts to define the boundary and accepted League intervention, arbitration, and mixed surveys, placing the dispute into a process that could examine one sector at a time. The campaign also showed that an Amazon frontier could not rest on ground patrols alone. River transport, aerial reconnaissance, aircraft supply, and dispersed posts had to support one another, while separate ammunition and food chains directly limited the speed of advance. The eventual outcome was not decided on the battlefield. Peru’s initiative in taking the dispute to an international forum converted armed contact into work for boundary commissions.
result: 直接軍事結果是沒有決定性勝負，也沒有投降或大規模割地。哥倫比亞未能突破至Iquitos，秘魯也未能切斷Putumayo上游的哥方據點；前哨控制大致回到戰前附近，戰事因而以有限軍事成果停滯。真正決定後續走向的是秘魯向國際聯盟提出交涉、哥倫比亞接受仲裁，以及兩國同意以混合委員會劃界。1933年1月24日的《里約議定書》沒有在談判桌上畫完整條邊界，卻啟動了實地測量、地圖製作與界標設置，針對Putumayo、Tabatinga等段落逐步處理。這條程序延續多年，並非1933年便宣告全部爭議消失；亞馬遜邊界的最終劃定直到1971年才完成。因此，這場戰爭的結果應寫成「邊界狀態大致維持、軍事勝負未決，爭議轉由國際仲裁與技術劃界處理」，而不是把任何一方的暫時奪哨視為永久主權取得。
resultEn: The immediate military result was neither a decisive victory nor a surrender or large territorial cession. Colombia failed to break through to Iquitos, and Peru failed to cut off the Colombian positions along the upper Putumayo. Control of the outposts returned approximately to the prewar pattern, and the fighting stalled with limited military gains. What shaped the aftermath was Peru’s referral of the dispute to the League of Nations, Colombia’s acceptance of arbitration, and the two states’ agreement to demarcate the frontier through mixed commissions. The Rio Protocol of January 24, 1933 did not draw the entire boundary in a conference room; it initiated field surveys, map preparation, and the setting of markers for sectors including Putumayo and Tabatinga. That process continued for many years rather than making every dispute disappear in 1933, and the Amazon boundary was not finally demarcated until 1971. The proper result is therefore a broadly maintained military status quo, no decisive battlefield outcome, and a dispute transferred from combat to international arbitration and technical boundary demarcation, rather than treating any temporary occupation of an outpost as permanent acquisition of sovereignty.
